records.source: אַחַ֣ר׀הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה הָיָ֤ה דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֶל־אַבְרָ֔ם בַּֽמַּחֲזֶ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אַל־תִּירָ֣א אַבְרָ֗ם אָנֹכִי֙ מָגֵ֣ן לָ֔ךְ שְׂכָרְךָ֖ הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: After these things came [the] word of YHWH to Abram in a vision, saying, do not fear, Abram; I [am] a shield to you; your reward [will be] very great.
pieces: Some time later the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Abram in a vision: "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, and your reward will be very great."

L.1: After these things the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Abram in a vision, saying, "Do not fear, Abram; I [am] a shield to you; your reward [will be] very great."

R.1: Some time later {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Abram in a vision. He said, "Do not be afraid, Abram. I will protect you like a shield, and I will reward you greatly."

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came ... in a vision: the language of prophecy
decisions.reason: "The word of the LORD came to" is how the prophets describe God speaking to them (Jeremiah 1:2; Hosea 1:1). Abram is later called a prophet (20:7).

decisions.choice: a shield: protection
decisions.reason: God promises protection after Abram's battle (chapter 14). The word (magen) echoes "delivered" (miggen) in 14:20.

decisions.choice: your reward will be very great
alternatives: I am your shield, your very great reward
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can mean that Abram's reward will be great, or that God himself is his very great reward. Having refused the spoils (14:22-24), Abram is promised a greater reward from God; the next verse shows he understands it as the gift of a son.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} makes a covenant with Abram

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְרָ֗ם אֲדֹנָ֤י יֱהוִה֙ מַה־תִּתֶּן־לִ֔י וְאָנֹכִ֖י הוֹלֵ֣ךְ עֲרִירִ֑י וּבֶן־מֶ֣שֶׁק בֵּיתִ֔י ה֖וּא דַּמֶּ֥שֶׂק אֱלִיעֶֽזֶר׃
records.gloss: And said Abram, my Lord YHWH, what will you give me, and I [am] going childless, and the heir of my house, he [is] Damascus Eliezer?
pieces: But Abram answered, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, what will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give me? I am still childless, and everything I have will go to Eliezer of Damascus."

L.2: And Abram said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, what will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give me, since I go on childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?"

R.2: But Abram said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, what good is any reward when I have no children? The one who will get everything I own when I die is Eliezer of Damascus."

decisions.choice: my Lord, the LORD: Adonai YHWH
decisions.reason: Abram addresses God as "my Lord" (adonai), followed by the divine name. It is the language of respectful prayer.

decisions.choice: the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus
alternatives: the son of possession of my house
decisions.reason: The phrase is obscure; it may mean "the one who will possess my house". The word for it (mesheq) sounds like Damascus (Dammeseq). The point is clear: without a son, Abram's estate will pass to a member of his household. Ancient custom allowed a childless man to adopt a servant as heir.

decisions.choice: Lord GOD (default); Lord Yahweh (divine name setting)
decisions.reason: When the divine name follows "Lord", English Bibles by long custom write "Lord GOD" in capitals, rather than "Lord LORD". The divine name setting gives "Lord Yahweh". "You" addressed to God takes the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְרָ֔ם הֵ֣ן לִ֔י לֹ֥א נָתַ֖תָּה זָ֑רַע וְהִנֵּ֥ה בֶן־בֵּיתִ֖י יוֹרֵ֥שׁ אֹתִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Abram, behold, to me not you have given offspring, and behold, a son of my house [is] inheriting me.
pieces: Abram went on, "Since {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have not given me a child, someone born in my household will inherit from me."

L.3: And Abram said, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given me no offspring, and so a member of my household will be my heir."

R.3: Abram said, "You have not given me any children, so one of my servants will get everything I own."

decisions.choice: a son of my house: someone born in my household
decisions.reason: "Son of my house" means a member of the household, such as a servant born there (14:14), not Abram's own child.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֨ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א יִֽירָשְׁךָ֖ זֶ֑ה כִּי־אִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵצֵ֣א מִמֵּעֶ֔יךָ ה֖וּא יִֽירָשֶֽׁךָ׃
records.gloss: And behold, [the] word of YHWH [came] to him, saying, not will inherit you this [one]; but [one] who will come out from your inward parts, he will inherit you.
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to him: "No, he will not inherit from you. Your heir will be your own son, born of your own body."

L.4: And look, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to him: "This man will not be your heir; one who will come out from your own body, he will be your heir."

R.4: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "Your servant will not get your things. You will have a son of your own, and he will get everything."

decisions.choice: who will come out from your inward parts: your own son
decisions.reason: The phrase means a child of Abram's own body (2 Samuel 7:12).

records.source: וַיּוֹצֵ֨א אֹת֜וֹ הַח֗וּצָה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַבֶּט־נָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֗יְמָה וּסְפֹר֙ הַכּ֣וֹכָבִ֔ים אִם־תּוּכַ֖ל לִסְפֹּ֣ר אֹתָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ כֹּ֥ה יִהְיֶ֖ה זַרְעֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And he brought him outside and said, look, please, to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able to count them. And he said to him, so will be your offspring.
pieces: He led Abram outside and said, "Look up into the sky and try counting the stars, if you can." Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told him, "Your descendants will be like that."

L.5: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought him outside and said, "Look toward the heavens and count the stars, if you are able to count them." And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "So shall your offspring be."

R.5: Then God took Abram outside and said, "Look up at the sky and count the stars, if you can. You will have as many descendants as that."

decisions.choice: count the stars: offspring beyond counting
decisions.reason: As with the dust of the earth (13:16), the promise is of numbers no one can count (22:17; Hebrews 11:12).

records.source: וְהֶאֱמִ֖ן בַּֽיהוָ֑ה וַיַּחְשְׁבֶ֥הָ לּ֖וֹ צְדָקָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he believed in YHWH, and he counted it to him [as] righteousness.
pieces: Abram put his trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} counted it to his credit as righteousness.

L.6: And he believed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} counted it to him [as] righteousness.

R.6: Abram believed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} accepted Abram as righteous because he believed.

decisions.choice: believed: trusted, relied on God's word
decisions.reason: The verb (he'emin) means to consider reliable and to lean on it: Abram took God at his word, though nothing he could see supported it.

decisions.choice: he counted it to him as righteousness: God accepted Abram as right with him
alternatives: Abram counted it (the promise) as God's righteousness
decisions.reason: The natural reading is that the LORD counted Abram's faith as righteousness. Some read Abram as the subject, counting the promise as God's justice. Paul and James both quote the verse with the first meaning (Romans 4:3; Galatians 3:6; James 2:23).

decisions.choice: righteousness: being in the right with God
decisions.reason: The word means right conduct, or standing in the right, in a right relationship (Deuteronomy 6:25). Here it is God's verdict on Abram, given because he believed.

decisions.choice: put his trust in ... counted it to his credit
alternatives: believed ... credited it to him as righteousness
decisions.reason: Balanced says "put his trust in" to bring out the sense of the verb (m1); Literal and Readable keep "believed", the word the New Testament uses when it quotes the verse.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑יו אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר הוֹצֵאתִ֨יךָ֙ מֵא֣וּר כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים לָ֧תֶת לְךָ֛ אֶת־הָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And he said to him, I [am] YHWH who brought you out from Ur of [the] Chaldeans to give to you this land to possess it.
pieces: He also told him, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to be your own."

L.7: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who brought you out from Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess."

R.7: He also said to Abram, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I brought you out of Ur in Chaldea to give you this land to be your own."

decisions.choice: I am the LORD who brought you out: the words that open the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: God introduces himself as he will at Sinai: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt" (Exodus 20:2). Abram's journey from Ur is the first exodus.

records.source: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יֱהוִ֔ה בַּמָּ֥ה אֵדַ֖ע כִּ֥י אִֽירָשֶֽׁנָּה׃
records.gloss: And he said, my Lord YHWH, how will I know that I will possess it?
pieces: But Abram said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, how can I be sure that I will possess it?"

L.8: And he said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, how will I know that I will possess it?"

R.8: But Abram asked, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, how can I be sure that this land will belong to me?"

decisions.choice: how will I know: asking for a sign, not doubting
decisions.reason: Abram has just believed (verse 6). His question asks for assurance, and God answers it with a covenant.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו קְחָ֥ה לִי֙ עֶגְלָ֣ה מְשֻׁלֶּ֔שֶׁת וְעֵ֥ז מְשֻׁלֶּ֖שֶׁת וְאַ֣יִל מְשֻׁלָּ֑שׁ וְתֹ֖ר וְגוֹזָֽל׃
records.gloss: And he said to him, bring me a heifer three years old, and a goat three years old, and a ram three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.
pieces: He answered, "Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat and a three-year-old ram, with a turtledove and a young pigeon."

L.9: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove and a young pigeon."

R.9: God said to him, "Bring me a young cow, a female goat and a ram, each three years old, and a dove and a young pigeon."

decisions.choice: the animals: those later used in Israel's sacrifices
decisions.reason: These are the kinds of animals the law of Moses later prescribes for sacrifice. Here they are used to make a covenant.

records.source: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֣וֹ אֶת־כָּל־אֵ֗לֶּה וַיְבַתֵּ֤ר אֹתָם֙ בַּתָּ֔וֶךְ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אִישׁ־בִּתְר֖וֹ לִקְרַ֣את רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְאֶת־הַצִפֹּ֖רלֹ֥א בָתָֽר׃
records.gloss: And he brought to him all these, and cut them in the middle, and set each piece opposite its neighbor; and the birds he did not cut.
pieces: Abram brought them all, split each one down the middle and laid the halves facing each other, but he did not split the birds.

L.10: And he brought him all these, and cut them in two, and laid each half opposite the other; but the birds he did not cut in two.

R.10: Abram brought all these animals, cut them in half and laid the halves in two rows facing each other. But he did not cut the birds in half.

decisions.choice: cut in two, each half opposite the other: a covenant ritual
decisions.reason: In an ancient covenant the parties walked between the halves of slaughtered animals, as if to say "may I be cut in two like these if I break this covenant" (Jeremiah 34:18-20). Hebrew speaks of "cutting" a covenant (verse 18).

records.source: וַיֵּ֥רֶד הָעַ֖יִט עַל־הַפְּגָרִ֑ים וַיַּשֵּׁ֥ב אֹתָ֖ם אַבְרָֽם׃
records.gloss: And came down the birds of prey on the carcasses, and drove them away Abram.
pieces: When birds of prey swooped down on the carcasses, Abram chased them off.

L.11: And birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.

R.11: Vultures came down to eat the dead animals, but Abram chased them away.

decisions.choice: birds of prey: a threat to the covenant
decisions.reason: Abram guards the offering. Some see in the birds a picture of the threats to the promise; the text does not explain them.

records.source: וַיְהִ֤י הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ לָב֔וֹא וְתַרְדֵּמָ֖ה נָפְלָ֣ה עַל־אַבְרָ֑ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵימָ֛ה חֲשֵׁכָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה נֹפֶ֥לֶת עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And it was, the sun [was] about to go, and a deep sleep fell on Abram; and behold, dread, darkness great, falling on him.
pieces: When the sun was going down, a deep sleep came over Abram, and with it a great and terrifying darkness.

L.12: And as the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell on Abram; and look, a dread and great darkness fell on him.

R.12: As the sun was going down, Abram fell into a deep sleep. A terrible darkness came over him, and he was very afraid.

decisions.choice: a deep sleep: the sleep of 2:21
decisions.reason: The word is the one used when God made the woman from the man (2:21): a sleep sent by God, in which he acts or speaks.

decisions.choice: dread, great darkness: terror at God's presence
decisions.reason: The dread is the fear that comes with God's nearness, and perhaps a foretaste of the dark years he is about to announce.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאַבְרָ֗ם יָדֹ֨עַ תֵּדַ֜ע כִּי־גֵ֣ר׀יִהְיֶ֣ה זַרְעֲךָ֗ בְּאֶ֨רֶץ֙ לֹ֣א לָהֶ֔ם וַעֲבָד֖וּם וְעִנּ֣וּ אֹתָ֑ם אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to Abram, knowing you shall know that a sojourner will be your offspring in a land not theirs, and they will serve them and they will afflict them four hundred years.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "You must understand that your descendants will be foreigners in a land that is not theirs. They will be enslaved and oppressed for 400 years.

L.13: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to Abram, "Know for certain that your offspring will be sojourners in a land that is not theirs, and they will be slaves there and be afflicted for 400 years.

R.13: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "I want you to know that your descendants will live as foreigners in a land that does not belong to them. The people there will make them slaves and treat them badly for 400 years.

decisions.choice: a land not theirs, slaves, afflicted: the years in Egypt
decisions.reason: God foretells Israel's slavery in Egypt (Exodus 1:11-12), using the words of the exodus story: "serve" and "afflict".

decisions.choice: 400 years: a round number
decisions.reason: Exodus 12:40 gives 430 years; Acts 7:6 repeats 400. The number is a round figure for the long stay. Verse 16 counts it as four generations.

decisions.choice: the LORD said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker; Literal keeps "he".

decisions.choice: slaves (L), enslaved (B), make them slaves (R)
decisions.reason: Kept at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt (m1).

records.source: וְגַ֧ם אֶת־הַגּ֛וֹי אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲבֹ֖דוּ דָּ֣ן אָנֹ֑כִי וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֥ן יֵצְא֖וּ בִּרְכֻ֥שׁ גָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And also the nation that they will serve I will judge, and afterward they will come out with possessions great.
pieces: But I will bring judgment on the nation that enslaves them, and afterward they will come out with great wealth.

L.14: But I will judge the nation that they serve, and afterward they will come out with great possessions.

R.14: But I will punish the nation that makes them slaves. Afterward your descendants will leave that land with great riches.

decisions.choice: judge: bring judgment on
decisions.reason: God will judge the nation, Egypt, by the plagues (Exodus 6:6; 12:12). The "great possessions" recall Israel leaving Egypt with gifts from the Egyptians (Exodus 12:35-36).

decisions.choice: enslaves (B), makes them slaves (R)
decisions.reason: Kept in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt (verse 13); Literal has "serve".

records.source: וְאַתָּ֛ה תָּב֥וֹא אֶל־אֲבֹתֶ֖יךָ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם תִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּשֵׂיבָ֥ה טוֹבָֽה׃
records.gloss: And you, you will go to your fathers in peace; you will be buried in old age good.
pieces: As for you, you will join your ancestors in peace and be buried at a ripe old age.

L.15: As for you, you will go to your fathers in peace; you will be buried at a good old age.

R.15: But you will die in peace when you are very old and be buried.

decisions.choice: go to your fathers: die, and join those who died before
decisions.reason: The phrase speaks of death as joining one's ancestors (25:8). Abram himself will not see the slavery or the return.

records.source: וְד֥וֹר רְבִיעִ֖י יָשׁ֣וּבוּ הֵ֑נָּה כִּ֧י לֹא־שָׁלֵ֛ם עֲוֺ֥ן הָאֱמֹרִ֖י עַד־הֵֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: And [the] generation fourth will return here, for not complete [is the] iniquity of the Amorite[s] until now.
pieces: Your descendants will return here in the fourth generation, because the Amorites' wickedness has not yet run its full course."

L.16: And in the fourth generation they will come back here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete."

R.16: After four generations your descendants will come back here. I will wait until then, because the Amorites who live here have not yet become so evil that they must be punished."

decisions.choice: the fourth generation: a long lifetime-length period
decisions.reason: A generation here may be a long period (about a hundred years), matching the 400 years of verse 13.

decisions.choice: the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete: God's patience and justice
decisions.reason: God will give the land to Abram's descendants only when its people's sin has reached its full measure (Leviticus 18:24-28). The delay shows both his patience with the Amorites and the justice of the later conquest.

decisions.choice: I will wait until then, because
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what the delay means (m2).

records.source: וַיְהִ֤י הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ בָּ֔אָה וַעֲלָטָ֖ה הָיָ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה תַנּ֤וּר עָשָׁן֙ וְלַפִּ֣יד אֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָבַ֔ר בֵּ֖ין הַגְּזָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And it was, the sun had gone and darkness was, and behold, a pot of smoke and a torch of fire which passed between these pieces.
pieces: After sunset, in the dark, a smoking fire pot and a blazing torch passed between the halves of the animals.

L.17: And when the sun had gone down and it was dark, look, a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch passed between these pieces.

R.17: After the sun had gone down and it was dark, a pot full of smoke and a burning torch appeared. They moved between the halves of the animals.

decisions.choice: a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch: signs of God's presence
decisions.reason: Smoke and fire mark God's presence, as later at Sinai and in the pillar of cloud and fire (Exodus 13:21; 19:18).

decisions.choice: passed between these pieces: God alone binds himself
decisions.reason: Only God's presence passes between the pieces; Abram does not. God takes the whole obligation of the covenant on himself, as if to say "may I be torn apart if I do not keep my word".

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא כָּרַ֧ת יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־אַבְרָ֖ם בְּרִ֣ית לֵאמֹ֑ר לְזַרְעֲךָ֗ נָתַ֨תִּי֙ אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את מִנְּהַ֣ר מִצְרַ֔יִם עַד־הַנָּהָ֥ר הַגָּדֹ֖ל נְהַר־פְּרָֽת׃
records.gloss: On that day cut YHWH with Abram a covenant, saying, to your offspring I give this land, from [the] river of Egypt to the river the great, [the] river Euphrates,
pieces: That day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made a covenant with Abram: "I am giving this land to your descendants, from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates,

L.18: On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made a covenant with Abram, saying, "To your offspring I give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:

R.18: On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made a covenant with Abram. He said, "I am giving this land to your descendants, from the river at the border of Egypt to the great Euphrates River.

decisions.choice: cut a covenant: made a covenant
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "cut" a covenant, from the ritual of cutting animals (verse 10).

decisions.choice: I give: a gift made as God speaks
decisions.reason: The completed verb form announces the gift as settled, as in 1:29 and 9:13.

decisions.choice: from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates: the widest borders of the land
decisions.reason: "The river of Egypt" may be the Nile or, more likely, the wadi on Egypt's border with Canaan (Numbers 34:5). The borders reached their fullest under David and Solomon (1 Kings 4:21).

decisions.reason: The list of ten peoples (verses 19-21) is the longest of its kind, a way of saying "everyone who lived there".
